Germ cell malignancy arising in the ovary, a reproductive site outside the axes; no endocrine dysfunction is established.

Carcinoma arising in the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Hereditary bipolar mood disorder is psychiatric; the broad neurological ancestor does not establish neurologic organ damage.
Thiamine deficiency defines the metabolic disorder; peripheral neuropathy and cardiac dysfunction define its major dry and wet forms.
Inherited cystic kidney disease with renal fibrosis and insufficiency; hypertension in 9/18 is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than direct vascular disease.
Acromesomelic skeletal dysplasia; complete atrioventricular block occurs in 1/2 annotated patients, supporting cardiac involvement with substantial small-cohort uncertainty.
Mitochondrial neuropathy with respiratory-chain dysfunction; fixed pes cavus affects 37/44 (~84%). Neurogenic bladder occurs in only 1/44 and is excluded.
